scene_timeline.visual_description: Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a white man with short grey hair, is shown speaking passionately at a Senate hearing, wearing a blue suit and a patterned gold tie. He is seated at a wooden desk with a microphone.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis states, "We expect exceptional leadership. And you've demonstrated anything but that. Time, after time, after time, I've been disappointed. I have reason to believe that you're violating the law, either knowingly or unknowingly."
scene_timeline.text_on_screen: REPUBLICAN SENATOR TEARS INTO KRISTI NOEM

scene_timeline.visual_description: Kristi Noem, a white woman with long brown hair, is shown speaking at a Senate hearing, wearing a dark blazer and large hoop earrings. A nameplate is visible in front of her.
scene_timeline.audio_description: A voice says, "Senator—" and then Kristi Noem states, "No. That $100,000 only had to do—"

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis is again shown speaking at the hearing, looking directly at the camera.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis says, "I will hold the clock until I finish."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis continues to speak with emphasis, gesturing with his hands, expressing frustration and disappointment.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis states, "We just want numbers. We want a thousand a day. 6,000 a day, 9,000 a day. Because numbers matter, right? No, they don't matter. Quality matters, not quantity. Quality. And what we've seen is a disaster, under your leadership, Mrs. Noem. A disaster."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis maintains an intense expression while speaking, occasionally looking to the side.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis says, "What we've seen is innocent people getting detained that turn out are American citizens. I could talk about the culture that's been created here with, with Stephen Miller aiding and abetting."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis continues to speak with a serious and critical tone, gesturing with his hands to emphasize his points.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis states, "The fact that you can't admit to a mistake, which looks like, under investigation, is going to prove that Ms. Good and Mr. Pretty probably should not have been shot in the face and in the back. Not only should the FBI be investigating it, but every single law enforcement agency in that jurisdiction should be invited to it. Matter of fact, in Ms. Good's case, I think that they were even saying that maybe there wasn't even a need to do it in the DOJ. That is stonewalling. That's a failure of leadership. And that is why I've called for your resignation."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis speaks directly to the camera, maintaining a stern expression.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis says, "I read your book last week. The passage where you talk about killing a dog that was 14 months old. You decided to kill that dog because you had not invested the appropriate time and training, and then you have the audacity to go into a book and say it's a leadership lesson about tough choices."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis continues his critique, using hand gestures to underscore his points.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis states, "At that same lunch hour, you killed a goat and you killed the goat because you said it was behaving badly. You are a farmer. You don't castrate a goat, they behave badly. You should have probably done that before. But my point is, those are bad decisions made in the heat of the moment. Not unlike what happened up in Minneapolis."

scene_timeline.visual_description: Thom Tillis claps his hands together once and then continues speaking.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Thom Tillis says, "I don't want an applause. Please don't do that for me."

parsed_output.overall_summary: This video features Republican Senator Thom Tillis criticizing Kristi Noem, the Secretary of Homeland Security, during a Senate hearing. Tillis expresses deep disappointment in Noem's leadership, accusing her of violating the law and overseeing a "disaster" in federal immigration enforcement, including the detention of American citizens and the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. He also condemns Noem for including stories in her book about killing a 14-month-old dog and a goat, which she presented as "leadership lessons about tough choices." Tillis concludes by calling for Noem's resignation due to her perceived failures in leadership and judgment.
